english.title: Use / give / send a false certificate / declaration re registration of a birth / death
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing a

(A)_[certificate]_
(B)_[declaration]_

under or for the purposes of an Act relating to the registration of births or deaths to be false, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FALSIFICATION..),

(C)_[used the same as true]_
(D)_[gave the same as true to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(E)_[sent the same as true to another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1)(b) of the Perjury Act 1911.

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Statutory requirement for corroboration (section 13).
(ii) A prosecution on indictment for an offence against this section shall not be commenced more than three years after the commission of the offence. (section 4(2)).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
